mainTopic: Hidden, humble righteous people whose prayers brought rain and miracles: אבא חלקיה, חנן הנחבא, רבי יונה, and רבי יצחק בן אלישיב
overview: The amud finishes the story of אבא חלקיה, the grandson of חוני המעגל, whom the רבנן asked to pray for rain. He acts in ways that look odd or rude, then quietly prays on the roof with his wife, and the clouds rise first from her corner. When the scholars ask about each strange action, every answer shows honesty, care for others' property, modesty, or good sense. His wife's prayer came first because her צדקה of bread helps the poor right away, or because she prayed for sinners to repent. Next comes חנן הנחבא, who asked ה׳ for rain for the sake of the children and hid himself from honor. רבי זריקא then contrasts the pious men of בבל, who prayed for rain in public, with רבי יונה of ארץ ישראל, who prayed in total secret. Stories follow about his son רבי מני and the wonder-worker רבי יצחק בן אלישיב, whose words changed reality, until he gave that power up. The amud ends as a new story begins: רבי יוסי בר אבין leaves his teacher for רב אשי, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אבא חלקיה ignores the greeting and acts strangely on the road
steps.stepSummary: אבא חלקיה does not return the scholars' greeting. On his way home he carries wood and cloak on separate shoulders, goes barefoot except in water, and lifts his clothes in thorny areas.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not show them a friendly face. Toward evening, while gathering firewood, he carried the wood and hoe on one shoulder and his cloak on the other. The whole way he walked barefoot, but when he reached water he put his shoes on. When he reached shrubs and thorns, he lifted up his clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes a list of strange things the scholars saw אבא חלקיה do. These are set up now so the גמרא can explain each one later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every action here looks backward or odd: protecting a cloak instead of his body, wearing shoes only where they seem least needed. The story deliberately builds up puzzles that will be solved at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: Showed a friendly face; returned a greeting

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that אבא חלקיה was rude or strange. Each of these actions gets a good explanation later in the story.

phrases.english: But he did not show them his face (return their greeting).
Toward evening, as he was gathering firewood,
he carried the wood and the hoe on one shoulder,
and the cloak on the other shoulder.
The whole way he did not wear shoes,
but when he reached water he put on his shoes.
When he reached shrubs and thorns,
he lifted up his clothes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אַסְבַּר לְהוּ אַפֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the scholars sent to אבא חלקיה, describing what they saw.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא חלקיה behaves in a series of puzzling ways on his way home from work.

steps.title: Arriving home: the wife, the order of entering, and the bread
steps.stepSummary: His wife greets him dressed up, enters the house first, and he eats without inviting the scholars. He gives the younger child two pieces and the older child one.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached the town, his wife came out to meet him, dressed up. When he reached his house, his wife went in first, then he went in, and then the scholars went in. He sat and ate bread and did not say to the scholars 'Come, eat.' He divided bread among the children: one piece to the older one and two to the younger one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps adding more puzzling details, this time at home. These also will be explained later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not inviting guests to eat looks very impolite, and giving the younger child more seems unfair. The story is collecting more questions that the scholars will need answered.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife (literally 'the one of his house')

phrases.english: When he reached the town,
his wife came out to meet him, adorned.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מְטָא לְבֵיתֵיהּ, עַלַּת דְּבֵיתְהוּ בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: When he reached his house, his wife entered first,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר עָיֵיל אִיהוּ, וַהֲדַר עָיְילִי רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: then he entered, and then the Sages entered.
He sat and ate bread,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַר לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן תּוּ כְּרוּכוּ.
phrases.english: and he did not say to the Sages, 'Come, eat.'
He divided bread to the children,
to the older one, one piece, and to the younger one, two.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְטָא לְמָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of puzzling behaviors, now at his home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: More strange behavior: his wife greets him dressed up, he does not invite guests to eat, and he gives the younger child more bread.

steps.title: Praying for rain on the roof without taking credit
steps.stepSummary: אבא חלקיה understands why the scholars came and goes up to the roof with his wife to pray quietly. The clouds rise first from his wife's corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to his wife: I know the Sages came because of the rain. Let us go up to the roof and pray. Maybe הקדוש ברוך הוא will be appeased and rain will come, and we will not take credit for ourselves. They went up to the roof. He stood in one corner and she in another. The clouds rose first from his wife's corner.
steps.whatsHappening: Before the scholars even ask, אבא חלקיה quietly prays for rain with his wife so no one will credit him. The clouds come first from her side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His goal is humility: if the rain comes now, before he is asked, the scholars will not say it came because of him. The detail that the clouds came from his wife's corner hints that her prayer was answered first. Steps 14 and 15 explain why.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a true צדיק wants the good result, not the honor that comes with it.

phrases.english: He said to his wife:

phrases.aramaic: יָדַעְנָא דְּרַבָּנַן מִשּׁוּם מִיטְרָא קָא אָתוּ,
phrases.english: I know that the Sages have come because of the rain.
Let us go up to the roof and pray for mercy.

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר דְּמִרַצֵּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְיֵיתֵי מִיטְרָא
phrases.english: Perhaps the Holy One, Blessed be He, will be appeased and rain will come,
and we will not take credit for ourselves.
They went up to the roof.

phrases.aramaic: קָם אִיהוּ בַּחֲדָא זָוִיתָא, וְאִיהִי בַּחֲדָא זָוִיתָא,
phrases.english: He stood in one corner, and she stood in another corner.

phrases.aramaic: קְדוּם סְלוּק עֲנָנֵי מֵהָךְ זָוִיתָא דִּדְבֵיתְהוּ.
phrases.english: The clouds rose first from that corner of his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ לִדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the strange behaviors to the main event: the prayer for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא חלקיה and his wife pray in secret, and the clouds appear first from her corner.

steps.title: אבא חלקיה says the scholars no longer need him
steps.stepSummary: He asks the scholars why they came; they say they were sent to ask him to pray for rain. He answers that God has already sent rain, so they did not need him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came down, he said to them: Why did the Sages come? They said: The Sages sent us to the Master to pray for rain. He said to them: Blessed is God, Who did not make you need אבא חלקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה acts as if the rain has nothing to do with him. He thanks God that the scholars did not need his help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He asks a question he already knows the answer to, so that he can hide his role. His answer, 'you did not need אבא חלקיה,' completes the plan from the previous step to avoid taking credit.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master, a respectful way to say 'you'

phrases.english: When he came down, he said to them:
Why have the Sages come?
They said to him:
The Sages sent us to the Master
to pray for mercy for rain.
He said to them: Blessed is God,
Who did not make you need אבא חלקיה.
phrases.notes: He speaks about himself by name, as if he were someone else, to hide that the rain came because of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נָחֵית אֲמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the prayer: he comes down and denies any role in the rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא חלקיה says the rain came without him, so the scholars did not need him.

steps.title: The scholars ask him to explain his puzzling behavior
steps.stepSummary: The scholars say they know the rain came because of him, and ask him to explain the things that puzzled them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We know the rain came because of the Master. But let the Master tell us about these things that puzzle us:
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars do not accept his modest denial. This line sets up the next steps, where they ask about each strange action one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the story turns from describing the puzzles to solving them. Each puzzle from steps 1 and 2 will now get its own question and answer.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: יָדְעִינַן דְּמִיטְרָא מֵחֲמַת מָר הוּא דַּאֲתָא,
phrases.english: We know that the rain came because of the Master,
but let the Master tell us
these things that puzzle us:

steps.triggerLanguage: יָדְעִינַן דְּמִיטְרָא מֵחֲמַת מָר הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects his denial and opens the series of questions about his behavior.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: An explanation for each of his strange actions.

steps.title: Why he did not return their greeting
steps.stepSummary: He did not answer their greeting because he was a hired day worker and did not want to take time from his employer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why, when we greeted the Master, did the Master not return our greeting? He said to them: I was a day laborer, and I said: I will not waste time.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars ask about the greeting, and he explains he was working for someone else at that moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What looked like rudeness was really honesty. His time during the work day belonged to his employer, so even stopping to greet would have been taking what was not his.

keyTerms.meaning: A worker hired for the day

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously a worker must treat his employer's time.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי יָהֵיבְנָא לְמָר שְׁלָמָא
phrases.english: What is the reason that when we greeted the Master,
the Master did not return our greeting?
He said to them: I was a day laborer,
and I said: I will not stop working.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי יָהֵיבְנָא לְמָר שְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First question in the series, about the first puzzle from step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: As a day worker, he could not take time away from his employer.

steps.title: Why the wood and the cloak were on separate shoulders
steps.stepSummary: The cloak was borrowed to wear, not to carry wood on, so he kept the wood off it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did the Master carry the wood on one shoulder and the cloak on the other? He said to them: It was a borrowed garment. I borrowed it for this, and I did not borrow it for that.
steps.whatsHappening: They ask why he did not put the wood on top of his cloak. He explains the cloak was borrowed only for wearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting wood on the cloak would use it in a way the owner never agreed to. He protects someone else's property even in a small way.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי טַעְמָא דְּרָא מָר צִיבֵי אַחַד כַּתְפֵּיהּ
phrases.english: And what is the reason the Master carried wood on one shoulder
and the cloak on the other shoulder?
He said to them: It was a borrowed garment.
For this I borrowed it, and for that I did not borrow it.
phrases.notes: He means: I borrowed it to wear, not to carry wood on.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא דְּרָא מָר צִיבֵי אַחַד כַּתְפֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second question in the series, about how he carried the wood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the wood and cloak were kept apart.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cloak was borrowed for wearing, not for carrying loads.

steps.title: Why he wore shoes only in the water
steps.stepSummary: On dry ground he could see where he stepped, so he saved his shoes; in water he could not see, so he wore them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did the Master walk barefoot the whole way, but put on his shoes when he reached water? He said to them: The whole way I can see; in the water I cannot see.
steps.whatsHappening: They ask about the shoes, and he explains it is about being able to see what he is stepping on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On land he can avoid sharp things, so there is no reason to wear out his shoes. In water he cannot see the ground, so he needs the shoes to protect his feet.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא כּוּלַּהּ אוֹרְחָא לָא סָיֵים מָר מְסָאנֵיהּ
phrases.english: What is the reason the whole way the Master did not wear his shoes,
but when he reached water, he put on his shoes?
He said to them: The whole way I can see,
but in the water I cannot see.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כּוּלַּהּ אוֹרְחָא לָא סָיֵים מָר מְסָאנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third question in the series, about the shoes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he wore shoes only in water.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On land he can see and avoid danger; in water he cannot, so he needs shoes there.

steps.title: Why he lifted his clothes among the thorns
steps.stepSummary: His skin can heal if scratched, but a torn garment cannot, so he protected the clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why, when the Master reached shrubs and thorns, did he lift up his clothes? He said to them: This heals, but this does not heal.
steps.whatsHappening: They ask why he exposed his legs to the thorns, and he explains that skin heals but cloth does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He weighs the loss: a scratch on the body goes away, but a tear in a garment is permanent. So he chose the loss that fixes itself.
steps.whatToRemember: Every strange action of אבא חלקיה so far turns out to come from honesty with his employer, care for borrowed property, or careful thinking about loss.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי מְטָא מָר לְהִיזְמֵי וְהִיגֵי
phrases.english: What is the reason that when the Master reached shrubs and thorns,
he lifted up his clothes?
He said to them: This heals,
phrases.notes: 'This' is his skin, and the next 'this' is the clothing.

phrases.english: and this does not heal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי מְטָא מָר לְהִיזְמֵי וְהִיגֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth question in the series, about the thorns.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he protected his clothes instead of his body.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A scratched body heals, but a torn garment does not.

steps.title: Why his wife came out dressed up
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask why his wife came out dressed nicely when he returned to the city. He says it was so he would not look at other women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did your wife come out dressed up when you came into the city? He said: so that I would not set my eyes on another woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask אבא חלקיה about another puzzling thing they saw, and he explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wife dressed up to greet him on purpose. His eyes and thoughts would then stay with her and not wander to other women in the city. Something that looked like showing off was really about guarding his holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a polite way to address someone

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי מְטָא מָר לְמָתָא
phrases.english: What is the reason that when the Master reached the city
the Master's wife came out adorned?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא אֶתֵּן עֵינַי
phrases.english: He said to them: so that I will not set my eyes
upon another woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי מְטָא מָר לְמָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of questions the חכמים asked after the rain came.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why his wife came out adorned to meet him.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: So that he would not look at other women.

steps.title: Why his wife walked in first, then him, then the guests
steps.stepSummary: They ask about the order of entering the house. He says he did not yet know them well enough to leave them alone with his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did she go in first, then you after her, and only then us? He said: because I have not checked you out.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask why they were let into the house last, and אבא חלקיה explains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not know these visitors, so he did not want them to be alone with his wife even for a moment. Walking in between her and them prevented that. It was a careful protection of modesty, not a lack of respect for them.

phrases.english: What is the reason that she entered first,
and then the Master entered after her,
and only then we entered?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא בְּדִיקִיתוּ לִי.
phrases.english: He said to them: because you have not been checked by me.
phrases.notes: He means he does not know yet how trustworthy they are, so he would not leave them alone with his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא עָיְילָא הִיא בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question in the same list.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He had not yet checked them, so he would not leave them alone with his wife.

steps.title: Why he did not invite them to eat
steps.stepSummary: They ask why he did not invite them to his meal. He says there was not enough bread, and he did not want credit for an offer he could not really make.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why, when you ate bread, did you not tell us 'Come eat'? Because there was not much bread, and I said: I should not get credit from the Rabbis for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask why he ate without inviting them, and he explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was not enough bread to feed guests, so an invitation would have been an offer he could not really fill. It would have earned him thanks he did not deserve. His honesty went so far that he would not even take credit for an empty invitation.

keyTerms.meaning: a favor or credit for nothing

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects to the idea of גניבת דעת, creating a false impression, even through a polite gesture.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי כָּרֵיךְ מָר רִיפְתָּא
phrases.english: What is the reason that when the Master ate bread
you did not say to us: 'Come and eat'?
Because there was not much bread,
and I said: I should not take from the Rabbis
credit for nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי כָּרֵיךְ מָר רִיפְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question in the same list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he did not invite them to eat.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There was not enough bread, and he did not want undeserved credit.

steps.title: Why the younger child got more bread
steps.stepSummary: They ask why the older child got one piece and the younger got two. He says the older stays home, while the younger sits learning in the synagogue.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did you give the older child one piece of bread and the younger two? He said: this one stays at home, and this one sits in the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask about the unequal amounts of bread, and he explains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The older child is home all day and can eat whenever he gets hungry. The younger child spends his day in the synagogue learning, far from food, so he needs more at mealtime. The split was fair according to each child's need.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא יְהֵיב מָר לְיָנוֹקָא קַשִּׁישָׁא
phrases.english: What is the reason the Master gave the older child
one piece of bread and the younger one two?
He said to them: this one stays at home,
and this one sits in the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא יְהֵיב מָר לְיָנוֹקָא קַשִּׁישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question in the same list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the younger child received more bread.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The older is home and can eat anytime; the younger learns in the synagogue.

steps.title: Why the clouds came first from his wife's side
steps.stepSummary: They ask why the rain clouds rose first from his wife's corner. He says her צדקה helps the poor right away, because she gives bread, while his gift of money helps them only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did the clouds rise first from the corner where your wife stood, before your own cloud? Because a wife is at home and gives bread to the poor, so her help reaches them right away. I give money, and its help does not reach them right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask their final question, about the clouds, and אבא חלקיה gives a first explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread is ready-to-eat help, so a hungry poor person is fed immediately. Money still has to be used to buy food, so the help comes later. Her prayer was answered first because her kind of צדקה is more direct.

keyTerms.meaning: her benefit, the help she gives

phrases.english: And what is the reason the clouds rose first
from that corner where there stood
the Master's wife, before his own cloud?
Because a wife is found at home,
and she gives bread to the poor,
and her benefit comes quickly.
But I give money,
and its benefit does not come quickly.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא קְדֻים סְלוּק עֲנָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last question in the list; it connects back to the rain itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the clouds formed first on his wife's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her צדקה of bread helps the poor immediately; his money helps only later.

steps.title: A second reason: she prayed for the hooligans to repent
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: he prayed that the troublemakers near them would die, but she prayed that they would repent, and they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or another reason: there were hooligans in our neighborhood. I prayed that they should die, and she prayed that they should repent, and they repented.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה gives a second, different reason why his wife's prayer was answered first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both wanted to be rid of the evil, but in different ways. He asked for the sinners to be destroyed, while she asked for them to change. Her prayer was the kinder one and it came true, which shows her prayer had greater power.
steps.whatToRemember: All of אבא חלקיה's odd actions turn out to come from honesty, modesty, and care. His wife's prayer is answered even before his, because of her direct kindness and her prayer that sinners would repent instead of being destroyed.

phrases.english: Alternatively: those hooligans
who were in our neighborhood,
I prayed that they should die,
and she prayed that they should return in repentance
[and they repented].
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added by the corrected wording of the text.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: הָנְהוּ בִּירְיוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same question about the clouds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the clouds formed first on his wife's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She prayed for the hooligans to repent, while he prayed for their death, and her prayer came true.

steps.title: חנן הנחבא prays for rain for the children's sake
steps.stepSummary: A new story: חנן הנחבא, grandson of חוני המעגל. Children were sent to beg him for rain, and he asked הקדוש ברוך הוא to answer for the sake of the children.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנן הנחבא was the daughter's son of חוני המעגל. When the world needed rain, the Rabbis would send schoolchildren to him. They would grab the hem of his cloak and say: Father, Father, give us rain! He said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the World! Act for the sake of these children, who cannot tell the difference between the Father who gives rain and the father who does not give rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new short story about another grandson of חוני המעגל who could bring rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children called him 'Father' as if he could make it rain. He did not take that credit. He turned to ה׳, the true Father who gives rain, and asked Him to answer for the children's sake. Even his prayer shows humility.

phrases.aramaic: חָנָן הַנֶּחְבָּא בַּר בְּרַתֵּיה דְּחוֹנִי הַמְעַגֵּל הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Chanan HaNechba was the son of Choni HaMe'agel's daughter.
When the world needed rain,

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ מְשַׁדְּרִי רַבָּנַן יָנוֹקֵי דְּבֵי רַב לְגַבֵּיהּ
phrases.english: the Rabbis would send schoolchildren to him,
and they would grab him by the hem of his cloak,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אַבָּא, אַבָּא, הַב לַן מִיטְרָא!
phrases.english: and say to him: Father, Father, give us rain!
He said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם! עֲשֵׂה בִּשְׁבִיל אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: Master of the World! Act for the sake of these,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין בֵּין אַבָּא דְּיָהֵיב מִיטְרָא,
phrases.english: who cannot tell the difference between the Father who gives rain
phrases.notes: This 'Father' is ה׳, the one who really gives rain.

phrases.english: and the father who does not give rain.
phrases.notes: Here he means himself. He is only a person and cannot make rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָנָן הַנֶּחְבָּא בַּר בְּרַתֵּיה דְּחוֹנִי הַמְעַגֵּל הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story, after the story of אבא חלקיה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנן הנחבא humbly asked ה׳ to bring rain for the sake of the innocent children.

steps.title: Why he was called 'the Hidden One'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he was called חנן הנחבא and answers that he would hide himself in the lavatory.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was he called 'חנן הנחבא'? Because he would hide himself in the lavatory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the meaning of his name and explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name הנחבא means 'the hidden one'. He earned it because he used to hide himself in the lavatory. This fits the humble person we just saw in the story.

phrases.english: And why was he called 'Chanan HaNechba'?
Because he would hide himself
in the lavatory.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״חָנָן הַנֶּחְבָּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the name of the person in the story just told.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the name הנחבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He would hide himself in the lavatory.

steps.title: רבי זריקא's comparison: the pious men of בבל pray in public
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא tells רב ספרא to notice a difference between the great men of ארץ ישראל and those of בבל. When rain was needed, רב הונא and רב חסדא would gather together and pray openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא said to רב ספרא: Come and see the difference between the powerful men of ארץ ישראל and the pious men of בבל. The pious men of בבל are רב הונא and רב חסדא. When the world needed rain, they would say: Let us gather together and pray for mercy. Perhaps הקדוש ברוך הוא will be appealed to and bring rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story by setting up a comparison. This step gives only the first side, בבל, so that the next steps can show the contrast with ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pious men of בבל prayed as a group and in the open. Their words are humble ("perhaps"), but everyone could see them praying. This sets the stage for רבי יונה, who did the same thing completely in secret.

keyTerms.meaning: powerful ones, great men of strong spiritual power

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זְרִיקָא לְרַב סָפְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika said to Rav Safra:
Come and see what the difference is between
the powerful men of the Land of Israel
and the pious men of Babylonia.

phrases.aramaic: חֲסִידֵי דְבָבֶל רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: The pious men of Babylonia: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda,
when the world was in need of rain
they would say: Let us gather together and pray for mercy;
perhaps the Holy One, Blessed be He, will be appeased
and bring rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא חֲזִי מָה בֵּין תַּקִּיפֵי דְּאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל לַחֲסִידֵי דְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stories of חוני's grandsons, a new comparison story about praying for rain begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pious men of בבל, רב הונא and רב חסדא, prayed for rain openly and as a group.

steps.title: רבי יונה secretly goes out and prays for rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה tells his family he is going to buy grain. He then goes to a low, hidden place, covers himself in sackcloth and prays, and rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The powerful men of ארץ ישראל, for example רבי יונה, father of רבי מני: when the world needed rain, he would go into his house and say to them: Give me my sack, and I will go buy myself a זוז's worth of grain. When he went outside, he would stand in a deep, low place, as it says: 'Out of the depths I called You, ה''. He stood in a hidden place, covered himself in sackcloth, and prayed for mercy, and rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא shows the other side of the comparison. רבי יונה, one of the powerful men of ארץ ישראל, prays for rain in total secret.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the men of בבל, רבי יונה gives his family a cover story about buying grain, so nobody knows he is going to pray. He picks a low place because of the פסוק about calling to ה' from the depths. His prayer works right away.

keyTerms.meaning: sackcloth, worn when fasting and praying

phrases.english: The powerful men of the Land of Israel,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן רַבִּי יוֹנָה אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי מָנִי,
phrases.english: such as Rabbi Yona, the father of Rabbi Mani:
when the world was in need of rain,
he would go into his house and say to them:
Give me my sack,
and I will go and bring myself a zuz's worth of grain.
When he went outside,
he would go and stand in a deep place,
as it is written: "Out of the depths I have called You, O Lord" (תהלים 130:1),
and he would stand in a hidden place,
and cover himself with sackcloth, and pray for mercy,
and rain would come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּקִּיפֵי דְּאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּגוֹן רַבִּי יוֹנָה אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי מָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of רבי זריקא's comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יונה prayed for rain in total secret, and his prayer was answered.

steps.title: רבי יונה hides his miracle from his family
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יונה comes home empty-handed, his family asks about the grain. He says that since rain came, food will soon be plentiful, so there was no need to buy it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came home, they said to him: Did the master bring grain? He said to them: I thought, since rain has come, now the world will have plenty.
steps.whatsHappening: The story finishes by showing that רבי יונה kept his secret even at home. He never tells his family that the rain came because of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer is true, but it hides the real reason he came home with nothing. This finishes the contrast with בבל: there the prayer was public, while here even his own household never learned of the miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: the world will have relief and plenty

steps.whatToRemember: The difference between the pious men of בבל and the powerful men of ארץ ישראל is public prayer compared with completely hidden prayer. רבי יונה hid his greatness even from his own family.

phrases.english: When he would come home,
they would say to him: Did the master bring grain?
He said to them: I said to myself,
since rain has come,
now the world will have relief.
phrases.notes: He means grain will soon be plentiful and cheap, so there was no reason to buy it now.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה אָתֵי לְבֵיתֵיהּ אָמְרִי לֵיהּ אַיְיתִי מָר עִיבוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the רבי יונה story by showing how he kept his prayer hidden at home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יונה covered up the miracle with a true but modest explanation.

steps.title: רבי מני cries at his father's grave and is protected
steps.stepSummary: Members of the house of the נשיא were troubling רבי מני. He threw himself on his father's grave and cried out. Later their horses got stuck there until they promised to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: רבי מני, his son, was being troubled by the house of the נשיא. He threw himself down on his father's grave and said: Father, father, these people are troubling me. One day they were passing by there, and their horses' legs got stuck, until they took it upon themselves not to trouble him anymore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another story about the greatness of רבי יונה. Even after his death, his merit protected his son רבי מני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "And furthermore" tells us this story adds to the earlier praise of רבי יונה. The horses were stuck at the very grave where רבי מני had cried, so the people troubling him understood why and changed their ways.

phrases.english: And furthermore: Rabbi Mani, his son,

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ קָא מְצַעֲרִי לֵיהּ דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה.
phrases.english: was being troubled by members of the house of the Nasi.
He threw himself down on his father's grave

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַבָּא אַבָּא! הָנֵי מְצַעֲרוּ לִי.
phrases.english: and said to him: Father, father! These people are troubling me.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד הֲווֹ קָא חָלְפִי הָתָם,
phrases.english: One day they were passing by there,
phrases.notes: "There" means by the grave of רבי יונה.

phrases.english: and the legs of their horses got stuck
until they took it upon themselves
not to trouble him anymore.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ רַבִּי מָנִי בְּרֵיהּ הֲווֹ קָא מְצַעֲרִי לֵיהּ דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further story showing the power of רבי יונה, now acting through his son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The merit of רבי יונה protected רבי מני even after רבי יונה's death.

steps.title: רבי מני's rich in-laws become poor
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני complains to רבי יצחק בן אלישיב that his wealthy in-laws are troubling him. רבי יצחק says they should become poor, and they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: רבי מני was often found before רבי יצחק בן אלישיב. He said to him: The rich men of my father-in-law's house are troubling me. He said: Let them become poor. And they became poor.
steps.whatsHappening: Another "and furthermore" story about רבי מני. This time a great צדיק's words change the fortune of the people bothering him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מני's in-laws were using their wealth to make his life hard. רבי יצחק בן אלישיב's words alone made them poor right away. This sets up a twist in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: often found before him, a regular student

phrases.english: And furthermore: Rabbi Mani was often found
before Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elyashiv.
He said to him: The wealthy men of my father-in-law's house
are troubling me.
He said: Let them become poor. And they became poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ רַבִּי מָנִי הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְיָשִׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story about רבי מני being troubled, this time saved by his teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק בן אלישיב's words made רבי מני's troublesome in-laws poor.

steps.title: The poor in-laws pressure him, so they become rich again
steps.stepSummary: Now that they are poor, the in-laws pressure רבי מני for support. רבי יצחק says they should become rich again, and they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Now they are pressuring me. He said: Let them become rich. And they became rich.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a twist. Being poor made the in-laws a new burden, so the blessing is reversed and they become rich again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first fix made a new problem: poor relatives leaned on רבי מני for money. רבי יצחק's words worked just as quickly in the other direction. This shows how much power the words of a true צדיק had.
steps.whatToRemember: These stories praise the powerful men of ארץ ישראל. רבי יונה prayed in secret, his merit protected his son after his death, and the words of רבי יצחק בן אלישיב could change a family's fortune right away.

phrases.english: He said: They are pressuring me.
phrases.notes: Now that they are poor, they keep asking רבי מני for money.

phrases.english: He said: Let them become rich. And they became rich.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר קָא דָחֲקוּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the result of the previous step after it creates a new problem.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The in-laws' wealth was given back once their poverty became a burden on רבי מני.

steps.title: רבי יצחק makes רבי מני's wife beautiful
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני complains that his wife is not pleasing to him. רבי יצחק בן אלישיב asks her name, says 'Let חנה become beautiful,' and she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני said: The people of my house (my wife) are not pleasing to me. רבי יצחק asked: What is her name? He answered: חנה. רבי יצחק said: Let חנה become beautiful. And she became beautiful.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רבי מני and רבי יצחק בן אלישיב continues with a third request. This time רבי מני complains about his wife's looks, and רבי יצחק's words immediately make her beautiful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the pattern of steps 22-23: רבי מני complains, and רבי יצחק says one sentence that changes reality. Here the change is to a person's appearance instead of to wealth. Asking her name lets רבי יצחק speak about her directly.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not pleasing / acceptable to me
The people of my house; here he means his wife

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: לָא מִיקַּבְּלִי עֲלַי אִינָשֵׁי בֵּיתִי.
phrases.english: He said: The people of my house are not pleasing to me.
phrases.notes: רבי מני is still the speaker. 'The people of my house' is a polite way of saying his wife.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is her name?
חנה. Let חנה become beautiful.
And she became beautiful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: לָא מִיקַּבְּלִי עֲלַי אִינָשֵׁי בֵּיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third complaint by רבי מני to רבי יצחק בן אלישיב, in the same pattern as the in-laws story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק's word makes רבי מני's wife beautiful at once.

steps.title: The wife becomes haughty, so she is made plain again
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני complains that his now-beautiful wife acts haughtily toward him. רבי יצחק says she should go back to her plain looks, and she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני said to him: She is acting proud toward me. He said to him: If so, let חנה go back to her plain looks. And חנה went back to her plain looks.
steps.whatsHappening: The fix from step 24 brings a new problem: the beautiful wife now acts proudly toward רבי מני. רבי יצחק reverses his own words, and she goes back to how she looked before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same 'fix, then undo' pattern as the in-laws story in steps 22-23. Each change brings a new problem, and רבי יצחק simply undoes it. The story shows how easily רבי יצחק could change things, and also that such changes did not really solve רבי מני's problems.

keyTerms.meaning: She is acting proud / haughty toward me

steps.whatToRemember: In both רבי מני stories, the in-laws and the wife, רבי יצחק's word changes reality at once. Each time the change causes a new problem, and he undoes it.

phrases.english: He said to him: She is acting proud toward me.
He said to him: If so,
let חנה return to her plain looks,
and חנה returned to her plain looks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קָא מִגַּנְדְּרָא עֲלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The result of step 24 causes a new problem, and רבי יצחק reverses it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the beauty leads to pride, רבי יצחק's word returns the wife to her earlier looks.

steps.title: Two students ask for a prayer to become wise
steps.stepSummary: Two students ask רבי יצחק בן אלישיב to pray that they become very wise. He answers that he once had this power but sent it away.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two students who sat before רבי יצחק בן אלישיב. They said to him: Let the master pray for us that we become very wise. He said to them: It was with me, and I sent it away.
steps.whatsHappening: Another story about רבי יצחק בן אלישיב. Two students ask him to pray that they become very wise, and this time he says no. He explains that he once had this power but gave it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the stories where his prayers worked right away, this story shows the opposite: רבי יצחק no longer uses that power. He means that he used to be able to pray for changes like this, but chose to send that ability away.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master pray (literally, ask for mercy)
It was with me, and I sent it away

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק is not saying he never had this power. He is saying he did have it, and gave it up by his own choice.

phrases.english: There were these two students

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲווֹ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְיָשִׁיב,
phrases.english: who were sitting before רבי יצחק בן אלישיב.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: נִיבְעֵי מָר רַחֲמֵי עֲלַן
phrases.english: They said to him: Let the master pray for mercy for us
that we should become very wise.
He said to them: It was with me, and I sent it away.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the power to pray for changes like this. He once had it, but gave it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ תְּרֵי תַלְמִידֵי דַּהֲווֹ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְיָשִׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about the same רבי יצחק בן אלישיב. This time he refuses to use the power he showed in the earlier stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק says he once had the power to pray for such changes but sent it away, so he does not pray for the students' wisdom.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר אבין leaves his teacher for רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין used to learn often by רבי יוסי of יוקרת. He left him and came to learn by רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין was often found before רבי יוסי of יוקרת. He left him and came before רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story with new people. This line is only the setup: רבי יוסי בר אבין left his regular teacher and went to learn by רב אשי. The main part of the story comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are only told the background here: who his teacher was, and that he switched to a new one. The reason he left, and what happened by רב אשי, are told in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Often found before him; he regularly learned by him
And he came before him (to learn)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ
phrases.english: רבי יוסי בר אבין was often found
before רבי יוסי of יוקרת.
He left him, and came before רב אשי.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּמִן יוֹקֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story with new people, after the stories about רבי יצחק בן אלישיב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background for the next story: רבי יוסי בר אבין left רבי יוסי of יוקרת and went to learn by רב אשי.
